title: Garden soil‐based microbial fuel cell equipped with an amplification system coupled with a secondary PV‐assisted module: Utilization as eco‐sustainable electrical power supply for carbon monoxide gas sensor
content:
Abstract

Autonomous environmental telemetry requires continuous, maintenance-free power sources capable of driving commercial sensing electronics. This study reports the development of a self-powered bio-electrochemical sensing platform utilizing a garden soil-based microbial fuel cell (s-MFC) coupled with a hybrid power management system (PMS) to drive a commercial off-the-shelf (COTS) carbon monoxide (CO) gas sensor. Operating under a sub-volt thermodynamic limit, the raw s-MFC generated a steady-state open-circuit voltage of 0.5 V, governed by the extracellular electron transfer of indigenous electroactive bacteria. To overcome this voltage bottleneck and satisfy the 3.0 V nominal operating threshold of the commercial sensor, an ultra-low-power DC/DC boost converter was engineered. The PMS incorporates a high-efficiency switching network driven by an operational amplifier and an NE555 timer configured in an astable multivibrator topology, synergistically integrated with a miniature photovoltaic (PV) solar module to sustain the active control loop and mitigate internal power overhead. Continuous 15-day galvanostatic testing demonstrated that the hybrid PMS successfully achieved a 6-fold voltage amplification, delivering a regulated 3.0 V rail to the gas-diffusion sensor while yielding a 70% increase in overall energy harvesting efficiency. These findings validate the scalability of soil bio-electrochemical systems combined with hybrid solid-state power conditioning to achieve long-term energetic autonomy for terrestrial micro-telemetry networks.
